title: Video-SVD: Efficient Video Diffusion via Orthogonal Basis Composition
claim: Attention heads in video diffusion models show hybrid, mixed spatial-temporal behavior rather than a clean spatial-versus-temporal split.

description: Two side-by-side heatmaps show the temporal frequency of each attention head in Wan image-to-video diffusion transformers. Panel (a) is WAN-1.3B-I2V, with about 30 layers (y-axis) and 12 heads (x-axis). Panel (b) is WAN-14B-I2V, with about 40 layers and 40 heads. Each cell is coloured with the viridis scale from 0 (spatial, dark purple) to 1 (temporal, yellow). Most cells fall in the teal-green middle range of about 0.4 to 0.7. A few bright yellow or dark purple outliers are scattered with no clear pattern. Each panel has a title, axis labels (Layer Index, Head Index) and its own vertical colorbar labelled Temporal Frequency. The eye goes first to the bright yellow cells and then to the speckled, mosaic-like texture.

abstract: Video Diffusion Transformers (VDiTs) represent the state of the art in video generation but remain constrained by the quadratic complexity of dense self-attention. To address this attention bottleneck, we analyze the pre-softmax matrix ($QK^\top$) and reveal two key properties: (1) video attention exhibits an effective low-dimensional structure with rapid singular-value decay, and (2) real motion induces hybrid spatio-temporal patterns rather than rigid ``spatial vs. temporal'' layouts. Guided by these observations, we propose Video-SVD, a training-free and plug-and-play acceleration method that does not modify the original network parameters. Video-SVD learns checkpoint-adaptive orthogonal bases offline and, at inference time, replaces expensive dense attention computation with lightweight online subspace projection and basis composition. To preserve high fidelity, Video-SVD further employs layer-shared dual-stream residual modules to recover fine-grained content details and positional information. Across HunyuanVideo and Wan2.1 backbones, Video-SVD achieves significant end-to-end speedups while maintaining high visual quality, reaching 1.92$\times$ on HunyuanVideo, 1.75$\times$ on Wan2.1-1.3B, and 1.79$\times$ on Wan2.1-14B.
